chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Ḥanān, who said:
A man asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, while I was listening, about a virgin man who commits fornication after having married, and he committed fornication before consummating with his wife.
He عليه السلام said: “He is to be given one hundred lashes, his hair is to be shorn, he is to be banished from the town for one year, and separation is to be made between him and his wife.”

key_terms.الْبِكْرِ: a virgin man; here, one not previously having consummated intercourse
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِأَهْلِهِ: consummate the marriage with his wife
key_terms.يُجَزُّ شَعْرُهُ: his hair is to be shorn
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ مِائَةً: is to receive one hundred lashes
key_terms.يُنْفَى: is to be banished or exiled

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a married but non-consummated man who commits zina in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who had entered marriage but committed zina before consummating with his wife. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states the prescribed penalty as one hundred lashes, shaving the head, banishment for one year, and separation from his wife, showing a detailed ruling within Shia fiqh on ḥudūd and marital status.
